title: The Target Has More Than One Shape
source: Al-Ruweidi, Target Transcription Factor States, Not Pockets, Drug Discovery Online, August 21 2026

scenes.text: Every transcription factor is more than a folded structure. In the cell, it samples shapes, partners, and chromatin contexts that decide which genes respond.
A screen against one purified domain may find a binder. It cannot prove that a ligand redirects the regulatory state sustaining disease.
An allosteric site may appear briefly as a protein moves. A static structure suggests possibility; experiments must establish whether that opening controls function.
First, specify the proposed event. Break a dimer, exclude a coactivator, rescue a mutant fold, or change residence on DNA. These are different outcomes.
Then trace causality: engagement in living cells, a change in protein state, chromatin occupancy, target gene response, and a phenotype that survives rigorous controls.
Belzutifan binds H I F two alpha and disrupts its partnership with A R N T. This is a clinically validated mechanism, not simply a pocket discovered in isolation.
T E A D offers another regulatory pocket: a lipid-binding cavity. Palmitoylation inhibitors can suppress YAP T E A D signaling, but the mechanism and safety questions differ.
Mutant p fifty three reverses the objective. The Y two twenty C substitution creates a crevice and destabilizes the protein. Rezatapopt seeks to restore activity, not inhibit it.
Binding alone may still mislead. A related p fifty three mutation can bind the stabilizer without recovering cellular function under the conditions tested.
Reporter signals can fall because cells are stressed. Target-null controls, resistant alleles, and orthogonal measurements help distinguish a real mechanism from a persuasive false positive.
Effective unbound exposure matters. A beautiful affinity result is not enough if cells cannot reach the needed concentration, or if an alternative pathway restores signaling.
The question is not only whether a protein contains a pocket. It is which disease-sustaining regulatory state can be shifted, measured, and falsified.
